title: Extend Go products API in 3 steps: pagination, categories, and CSV export
description: Multi-step Go task: extend the legacy products API with pagination support, a category field with filtering, and a CSV export endpoint.

task_spec.prompt:
Extend internal/products/products.go in three steps. All 4 existing tests must still pass.

Step 1 — Pagination:
  Update GET /products to accept ?limit=N&offset=M query params.
  - If absent or invalid (non-integer), ignore (return all).
  - Slicing: store[offset:min(offset+limit, len(store))].
  - Return {"products": [...], "total": <total before pagination>}.
  - Existing GET /products must now return this shape (update listProducts).

Step 2 — Category field:
  Add Category string field to Product struct (json: "category").
  - POST /products body now accepts optional "category" (default empty string).
  - GET /products accepts optional ?category=X param: case-insensitive equality filter.
  - Category filter applies BEFORE pagination.

Step 3 — CSV export:
  GET /products/export
  - Content-Type: text/csv
  - First row: Name,Price,Category header
  - One row per product: {name},{price},{category}
  - Price formatted to 2 decimal places
  - No pagination applied; always exports all products
  - Must be routed before the /products/{id} catch-all in Handler

All 4 existing tests plus solution-only tests must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: GET /products/export returns CSV with Name,Price,Category header
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `go test ./...` to see where we stand. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.
Final push: run `go test ./...` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure the full implementation is complete and all tests pass.
